newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo hires Von der Heyden CFO for a year.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo hires Von der Heyden CFO for a year.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc. said Wednesday it appointed Karl M. von der Heyden chief financial officer and vice chairman for about one year to help formulate long-term growth strategy for the beverage giant and identify a successor.
Von der Heyden, who resigned as a non-executive director to take the post at Pepsi, will also be nominated for election to the board of directors.
He replaces Robert Dettmer, 65, who is retiring as executive vice president and CFO.
Von der Heyden, 60, has been an executive at leading consumer products companies for over 20 years, including six at PepsiCo, the Purchase, N.Y.-based company said.
Michael Branca, analyst at Lehman Brothers, said Von der Heyden's appointment is a "big plus" for PepsiCo.

"Clearly Pepsi's new chief financial officer brings tremendous depth of experience, having been involved with Cadbury Schweppes Plc, RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp., H.J. Heinz Co. and Pepsi in the past," he said.
Pepsi's stock rose 87.5 cents to $29.875 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the most active issue in early afternoon trading.
